case_name: Union of India and Others v Sushil Kumar Modi and Others
facts: This order has to be read in continuation of our order dated November 5, 1996 passed in Civil Appeal Nos. 14164-65 of 1996, Union of India & Ors. Vs. Sushil Kumar Modi & Ors., reported in 1996 Indlaw SC 1578.
The material facts need not be reiterated as they are mentioned in our aforesaid order dated November 5, 1996.

When the matter was taken up in the Patna High Court subsequent to our aforesaid order dated November 5, 1996, during the further proceedings after our order, the High Court has made the two orders dated November 13, 1996 and December 19, 1996.
The learned Attorney General, on behalf of the appellants, has indicated certain portions of these two orders and contended that they do not match with our earlier order dated November 5, 1996.
issues: What if the Director does not make the reference on his own.

The aforesaid aspects of the matter as also other aspects, which were briefly mentioned during the course of hearing today, can be more properly and effectively discussed in the presence of the Director, CBI, himself.
petitioner_arguments: These appeals by special leave are against some portions of the orders dated November 13, 1996 and December 19, 1996 passed by the Patna High Court in the same matter - CWJC No. 1617 of 1996 with CWJC No. 602 of 1996 - as a sequel thereto.

The learned Attorney General submitted that the above extracts of the two orders made by the High Court, in particular, are unwarranted apart from certain other observations therein which could have been avoided.
respondent_arguments: In reply Shri Ram Jethmalani submitted that the observations of the High Court have to be understood in the context as indicating the manner in which the Central Bureau of Investigation.
He submitted that a grievance of this kind by the CBI does not appear to be appropriate.
court_reasoning: The duty of the Court in such proceedings is, therefore, to ensure that the CBI and other Government agencies do their duty and do so strictly in conformity with law.

It has to be borne in mind that the purpose of these proceedings is essentially to ensure performance of the statutory duty by the CBI and the other Government agencies in accordance with law for the proper implementation of the rule of law.
The nature of such a proceeding in a Court of law was also indicated by Lord Denning, as under: 'A question may be raised as to the machinery by which he could be compelled to do his duty.'
